one_liner: Multi-buffer SHA-256 in Rust whose wasm simd128 build hashes small-message batches about 3.4-3.7x faster than @noble/hashes in V8.
what_it_does: tape-sha256 is a Rust crate (0.2.1 on crates.io) that hashes many independent messages per call (hash_many, hash_many_prefixed, hash_pairs for Merkle parents) and runs serial or parallel SHA-256 hash chains (hash_chain, hash_chains for Solana proof-of-history). For JavaScript, the repo ships only an example cdylib (examples/wasm_lib.rs) exporting walloc, backend_name and hash_many_prefixed_raw over linear memory: the caller copies message bytes and a length array into wasm memory, makes one call per batch and reads 32-byte digests back. It is not a drop-in for noble's sha256(bytes) one-shot; it is a batch interface and there is no npm package.
how_it_is_fast: SHA-256 cannot be vectorised within one message because each round depends on the last, so the crate runs four independent messages in lockstep, one per u32x4 lane of a wasm v128 register (multi-buffer hashing, as in Intel's isa-l_crypto). Input words are loaded with a byte-swapping i8x16 shuffle and transposed into lane order with canonical i32x4 shuffles that engines lower to single instructions; rotates are shift-pair plus or, since wasm has no vector rotate. The rounds are fully unrolled (flat-round body), and one wasm call amortises the JS-to-wasm boundary over the whole batch, which is what beats per-call libraries on 60-90 byte messages.
when_to_use: Hashing many small independent messages (about 60-100 bytes, two SHA-256 blocks) in a synchronous browser loop, such as Solana createWithSeed vanity-address grinding: 4.55 M candidates/s in Chrome 150, 3.7x noble and 1.6x hash-wasm.
Replacing @noble/hashes (the @solana/web3.js 1.x path) or hash-wasm for batched Merkle-leaf hashing in a JS runtime without native crypto, where you can collect leaves into one call.

Rust code (native, not wasm) that hashes Merkle leaves or verifies many hash chains: the same crate dispatches to AVX-512, SHA-NI, ARM SHA-2 and NEON multi-buffer kernels, 2.0-6.8x the sha2 crate in its BENCHMARKS.md.
Engines where the multi-buffer wasm kernel is known to help: V8 (Node, Chrome) and JavaScriptCore (Bun) per the repo's matrix.cjs runs.
when_not_to_use: Node.js: native node:crypto crypto.hash does the 64-leaf batch in 42.89 us against 100.61 us for the wasm build (2.3x faster, derived from page data); the author recommends a napi binding of the native backend instead.
Browser batches of ~1 KB messages: Chrome's WebCrypto subtle.digest with Promise.all measured 75 us against 80-90 us for the wasm build, and the README says to use WebCrypto there.
One message at a time or one large message: the speedup comes from filling four lanes per call; a single-stream hasher such as hash-wasm or WebCrypto fits better.
Solana PDA derivation: the ed25519 off-curve check is 94-99% of each candidate's cost, so batching the hashes gained only 4% (37.5 vs 39.1 us per PDA in Chrome).

Targets that must run on engines without wasm SIMD (Safari and iOS before 16.4, per Emscripten's SIMD docs found by search): a simd128 build is rejected at instantiation and there is no runtime fallback inside one module.

integration.form: crate (Rust); for JS, a self-built wasm32-unknown-unknown cdylib from examples/wasm_lib.rs, no npm package
integration.dependencies: none at runtime (sha2, rand and ed25519-dalek are dev-dependencies only); JS glue must be written by the user
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 (rust-version in Cargo.toml); wasm build needs RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+simd128' and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target
integration.platforms: wasm32 with simd128 (simd128-4 kernel); native x86-64 (AVX-512, AVX2, SHA-NI), aarch64 (ARM SHA-2, NEON), portable Rust fallback elsewhere
integration.thread_safety: Entry points are stateless; the crate docs say two threads may call them concurrently on disjoint halves of a batch. The crate never spawns or pins threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — produces bit-identical SHA-256 digests, but replaces noble's per-message sha256(bytes) with a batch call over wasm linear memory and JS glue you write yourself

gotchas: Stale fallback claim: benches/wasm/README.md says a build without +simd128 falls back to portable-8 and 'roughly ties hash-wasm', but current dispatch in src/lib.rs (changed in commit d967d91 'fix portable fallback width', 2026-07-27; BENCHMARKS.md agrees) picks portable-8 only on aarch64 and portable-1 on every other target including wasm32, so the non-SIMD wasm speed is not documented for the current code.

SIMD is a build-time fact in wasm (no runtime probing): ship two modules and feature-detect in JS if you need older engines. SpiderMonkey runs the 2x4 and 4x4 multi-wave kernels at 0.57-0.64x, so dispatch stays on the single 4-lane wave and Firefox gains are not measured beyond that.

The example module's walloc never frees memory and the bench module is about 210 KB because it exports three extra wave kernels; the author measured a dispatch-only build at 47.1 KB (38.7 KB after wasm-opt, 14.2 KB gzipped).

Benchmark reproducibility gaps: benches/wasm has no package-lock, so the exact @noble/hashes 1.x (^1.5.0; noble's current line is 2.4.0) and hash-wasm versions measured are not recorded; Node numbers are unpinned; Chrome's performance.now is clamped to 100 us, so batch rows move in 5 us steps and the grind rows (4 iterations of about 0.45 ms for tape) in roughly 5% steps, enough to blur tape vs WebCrypto at ~1 KB.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over sha2-wasm (single-stream SHA-2, about 5-7% faster than hash-wasm) when you hash many independent short messages per call, since multi-buffer lanes and one boundary crossing per batch give 1.55-1.6x over hash-wasm here; pick sha2-wasm or WebCrypto for one long stream. For Solana PDA work pair it with a faster curve check such as berith's wasm Ed25519, because the hash is only 1-6% of the cost.
verified_claims_summary: On an Apple M4 Max, a 64-leaf Merkle batch (67,680 bytes) in Node v24 took 100.61 us with the simd128 wasm build including copies in and out, against 337.97 us for @noble/hashes 1.x one-shot (about 3.4x) and 156.24 us for hash-wasm (1.55x), while node:crypto took 42.89 us; in Chrome 150 an 87-byte createWithSeed grind reached 4.55 M candidates/s against 1.22 M for noble (3.72x) and 2.82 M for hash-wasm (1.61x). Builds used rustc release with +simd128; best of 15 rounds x 50 iterations (Chrome: 12 x 20, grind 12 x 4) after warmup, with every tape lane checked against node:crypto or noble.
status_note: Active but very young (13 commits, 2026-07-26 to 2026-08-11, two committers, 1 star, 0 issues, crate 0.2.1 with 469 downloads); Apache-2.0 and small enough to vendor, but the JS integration is an example, not a maintained package.
